## YouTube: modular foundation video description

Target existing video: https://youtu.be/uP0rcGYw9Sw

SPORTENVO presents modular steel foundation bases for selected leased, flexible-site and relocatable padel projects. Modular does not mean no ground preparation: support conditions, levels, drainage, anchors, court loads and any roof loads still require review. Compare the confirmed court-to-foundation interface and project drawings, not only the advertised base dimensions.

## Medium: original educational article draft

Suggested title: Three questions that make padel court quotations easier to compare

Two proposals can show similar-looking courts and still describe different projects. Before deciding which price is better, establish what the buyer actually receives, what evidence supports it, and which work remains local.

### 1. Are both suppliers quoting the same site?

A premium indoor venue, an exposed coastal club and a leased property have different constraints. Give each supplier the same location, court quantity, venue dimensions, ground information, weather exposure and intended operating model. Mention roofs and future relocation at the beginning; both can change the foundation and installation boundary.

Choose the court concept after these inputs are understood. Open viewing does not remove structural responsibilities. A reinforced court label does not establish approval for a high-wind site. A modular foundation does not make drainage or bearing capacity irrelevant.

### 2. Can the quoted specification be checked?

Ask for the selected steel sections, corrosion protection, glass scope, turf, lighting, anchors and technical drawings. Match inspection and packing information to the actual order. Factory photographs can provide context, but the important question is whether the evidence relates to the configuration being quoted.

A completed project is useful for discussing layout, operation and site constraints. It is not proof that the same engineering assumptions apply to a new location. Request comparable references and a clearly stated supply scope rather than assuming that every photographed venue had the same delivery responsibilities.

### 3. What is excluded from the price?

Write down freight, import handling, unloading, civil works, foundations, drainage, electrical work, lifting, local installation, permits and engineering responsibilities. Clarify installation guidance and component-level warranty terms. These items may be included, excluded or assigned to different parties; only the actual proposal establishes the boundary.

Use the same scope table for every supplier. An inexpensive proposal may be suitable, but its value cannot be judged fairly if another supplier includes work that it excludes. The comparison should separate equipment cost from the full project budget.
